title: Maximum Length of Semi-Decreasing Subarrays
summary: Given an integer array, find the length of the longest subarray where the first element is strictly greater than the last element, or return 0 if no such subarray exists.
statement: Given an integer array, find the length of the longest subarray where the first element is strictly greater than the last element, or return 0 if no such subarray exists.
constraints: nums is nonempty and may contain negative values.
A subarray is semi-decreasing when its first value is strictly greater than its last value; interior order is irrelevant.
Return the greatest such length, or zero if none exists.
hints: Only an early large endpoint and a late smaller endpoint matter.
Keep indices of increasing prefix maxima, then scan right endpoints backward and pop every maximum that is larger.
Each popped index is paired with its farthest possible qualifying right endpoint.
A dominated earlier candidate is never useful; reverse scanning ensures the first successful pairing for each retained left index has maximum width.
